newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens Nixdorf sees higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Siemens Nixdorf sees higher sales.

text.p: German engineering giant Siemens AG said on Thursday it expects increased sales, orders and cost-cutting to lift profits next year at its Siemens-Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG (SNI) computers unit.
"SNI over the last three years made pretty good progress even if last year was not what we had hoped," Siemens chief executive Heinrich von Pierer said at the company's annual news conference.
"SNI has very god market positions in Germany where it's number one in PCs. It is number two or three in Europe in Unix systems and mainframes," he said.

Von Pierer said Siemens expected to cut about 6,000 domestic jobs in 1996/97, many of them at SNI. Personnel costs in Germany rose seven percent overall in 1995/96 as the computer unit struggled with sharp falls in prices and margins.
The group will need to continue reducing costs aggressively because its loss carry-forward for 1995/96, which ended September 30, was over two billion marks, Pierer said.
SNI reported 1995/96 pretax proft fell 16 percent to 52 million. The firgure was an anaemic 0.4 percent of sales.
